jobs.title: GIS Specialist – Environmental Consulting
jobs.description:
About Us

Confluence Compliance Companies, LLC (Confluence) is a growing team of environmental professionals based in the Rocky Mountains. We are employee-focused and committed to creating a flexible, supportive work environment that balances high-quality results with work-life balance.

At Confluence, you’ll find:

Competitive pay and benefits, including profit sharing.

A collaborative team that values adaptability and problem-solving.

Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.

A culture built on safety, communication, and continuous improvement.

We thrive in changing regulatory, social, and environmental landscapes and we’re looking for motivated, adaptable professionals to grow with us.

Description

Confluence is seeking a seasoned GIS Specialist to support our environmental consulting projects across the Rocky Mountain region. Unlike many GIS roles that only “produce maps,” this position is central to our enterprise GIS program and the success of our projects. You will enforce internal GIS standards, validate and manage incoming datasets, standardize workflows, and maintain our ArcGIS Online infrastructure and spatial data resources to maintain and improve on critical data analysis and reporting needs. Your work will directly support field operations, regulatory compliance, and client deliverables by producing high-quality analysis, figures, and interactive maps.

The ideal candidate excels in Esri platforms, enforces data quality standards, and integrates drone-collected imagery with environmental data for client-ready results. This role combines data architecture and workflow automation with the production of professional maps and graphics that directly support environmental assessments, permitting, and project management.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and enforce standardized GIS templates, symbology, and workflows across company projects.

Develop quality assurance plans to validate and quality control incoming spatial datasets and outgoing deliverables to ensure compliance with regulatory, client, and company standards.

Maintain and enhance the company’s ArcGIS Online spatial database, including data organization, permissions, and quality control.

Produce high-quality maps, figures, dashboards, and spatial analyses to support environmental assessments, regulatory submittals, and client deliverables.

Design and deploy Survey123 forms, field maps, and mobile applications to support field data collection and monitoring activities.

Integrate drone-collected ortho-imagery with Global Positioning System (GPS)-referenced field data for sub-meter to sub-inch precision mapping.

Support data automation by developing workflows that link laboratory results with field sample locations and other project datasets.

Collaborate with scientists, project managers, and field crews to integrate spatial analysis into project planning, compliance documentation, and client presentations.

Provide training, support, and licensing management for staff using ArcGIS products.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or related field.

3–7 years of professional GIS experience in environmental consulting, natural resources, or a related industry.

Demonstrated proficiency with Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated tools/platforms (Survey123, Field Maps, Dashboards).

Strong technical skills in geodatabase design, feature services, and data integration.

Solid grasp of projections, coordinate systems, datum transforms, spatial resolution, data accuracy, and Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC) principles.

Proficiency in data management and automation workflows (Python preferred).

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present spatial analysis to technical and non-technical audiences.

Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Must pass a standard background check.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Colorado Energy & Carbon Management Commission (ECMC), Wyoming Oil & Gas Conservation Commission (WOGCC), and Bureau of Land Management (BLM) regulatory environments.

Experience with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), Clean Water Act (CWA), and other applicable federal and state regulatory frameworks.

Professional GIS certification (GISP) or progress toward certification.

Experience with oil and gas projects, particularly upstream and midstream operations.

Demonstrated knowledge of spatial data standards and formats required by regulatory agencies.

Experience producing GIS deliverables for permitting, compliance reporting, or regulatory submittals.

Advanced Python scripting for automation and geoprocessing.

Experience with remote sensing and photogrammetry (drone/Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) data).

Proficiency with ArcGIS Online administration and web mapping services.

Background in environmental fieldwork, GPS data collection, or survey support.

Summary Job Description

We are currently recruiting a Marine Spatial Data Analyst to provide technical stewardship of Blue Ventures' spatial data system, ensuring the continued delivery of high-quality spatial data, dashboards and decision-support tools that support community-based fisheries management. This role will combine spatial data management, database administration, data visualisation and user engagement, while supporting marine spatial planning analyses and the development of user-centred decision-support tools.

Reporting to the Head of Spatial Ecology, this is a full-time remote role, with occasional international travel to work closely with colleagues, partners, field teams and communities.

Roles across the Data Science team are highly interdependent, and candidates must be equally comfortable working independently: competently driving their own tasks and team priorities, and thriving within a small, collaborative team. Given BV's global, distributed structure, applicants must demonstrate experience coordinating effectively across regions and cultures, with genuine sensitivity to differing working styles, communication norms, and paces of work. Culture of Care:

At the South Orange County Community College District (SOCCCD), we foster a Culture of Care grounded in connection, collaboration, inclusion, and service. We seek employees who contribute to a welcoming, student-centered environment and who understand the important role every position plays in advancing student success and strengthening our District community. Our employees build meaningful relationships, demonstrate empathy and professionalism, and promote a culture of belonging, engagement, and mutual respect.

Application Instructions:

•
Complete all sections and fields on the application and attach all required documents – incomplete applications may not be considered.
• Include all relevant education, training, and/or experience on the application.
• Do not include any personally identifiable, confidential, or otherwise unrequested information that does not pertain to job related factors (e.g., social security number, date of birth, pictures, etc.) on your application or attached documents.
• For job postings with a close date, all applications received by 11:59 PM (Pacific Time) on the job posting close date, will receive consideration.
• For job postings with an initial screening date, all applications received by 11:59 PM (Pacific Time) on the job posting initial screening date, will receive priority consideration; however, typically the job posting will remain open, and continue to accept applications, until the position is filled.

Description

Class specifications are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties performed by employees in the class. Specifications are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job.

SUMMARY DESCRIPTION

Under general direction from an appropriate level manager or administrator, serve as the coordinator for assigned program or project area providing professional level program or project area support and services; develop and provide a full range of program or project area functions or services including difficult administrative and management support duties in support of the assigned project, program, or functional area; provide direction for assigned programs, projects, or functional area; serve as a liaison between the program area and the general public, students, staff, and other campus and community officials and groups; develop and maintain relationships with other organizations and schools in the program, project, or functional area; and plan, coordinate, and implement assigned operations and activities of the assigned office.

REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES

The following duties are typical for this classification. Incumbents may not perform all of the listed duties and/or may be required to perform additional or different duties from those set forth below to address business needs and changing business practices.
• Coordinate and oversee the development and implementation of assigned aspects of the assigned project, program, or program area; ensure compliance with all aspects of program requirements including grant requirements.
• Plan, design, and implement program or project elements that support service delivery; participate in processes to define scope and schedule of services and activities; oversee and participate in implementation processes.

QUALIFICATIONS

The following generally describes the knowledge and ability required to enter the job and/or be learned within a short period of time in order to successfully perform the assigned duties.

Knowledge of:

• Pertinent federal, state, and local laws, codes, rules, regulations, policies, and procedures related to area of assignment.
• District and College organization, operations, policies, and objectives.

Ability to:

•
Learn and understand the organization and operation of the assigned department as necessary to assume assigned responsibilities; understand, explain, and apply administrative and office policies and procedures as well as pertinent laws, codes, regulations, and ordinances; work within the policies, functions, and requirements of area of assignment; assure compliance with State and federal laws and District policies.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE GUIDELINES

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the knowledge and abilities would be:

Education/Training:

Equivalent to a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in a public administration, business administration, or related field.

Experience:

Three years increasingly responsible professional experience related to program area of assignment.

License or Certificate:

A valid California driver’s license and proof of insurability may be required for some positions to drive a District or personal vehicle to attend meetings or pick up/deliver documents or other materials.

California Public Employees Retirement System and California State Teachers Retirement System:

A California Public Employees Retirement System (CalPERS) retiree may not accept employment until after the first 180 days of retirement. Anyone retired from CalPERS accepting permanent employment with the SOCCCD will be required to reinstate as an active CalPERS member. Please contact CalPERS for additional information regarding your retirement status.

Any active vested member of California State Teachers Retirement System (CalSTRS), who accepts employment with the SOCCCD to perform service that requires membership in CalPERS, is eligible to elect to continue retirement system coverage under CalSTRS

Non-Discrimination Notice:

The SOCCCD provides access to its services, classes, and programs without regard to national origin, immigration status, religion, age, gender, gender identity, gender expression, race, ethnicity, color, medical condition, military and veteran status, genetic information, ancestry, sexual orientation, marital status, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, or because they are perceived to have one or more of the foregoing characteristics, or based on association with a person or group with one or more of these actual or perceived characteristics.

California Fair Chance Act:

The SOCCCD will consider qualified applicants with a criminal history pursuant to the California Fair Chance Act. You do not need to disclose your criminal history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if the SOCCCD is concerned about a conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Equal Employment Opportunity:

The SOCCCD is looking for equity and inclusion-minded applicants who represent the full diversity of California and who demonstrate a sensitivity to the understanding of diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds present within our community.

The SOCCCD is committed to ensuring that all students have the opportunity to succeed in their classes and as such, to eliminating institutional barriers that disproportionately impact students of color. Irvine Valley College and Saddleback College are deeply committed to fostering an inclusive environment where students, staff, and faculty from diverse backgrounds can thrive academically and professionally.

Irvine Valley College (IVC) serves approximately 21,584 students, reflecting a rich diversity: 41% Asian, 2% Black/African-American, 21% Hispanic/Latino, 8% Southwest Asian and North African, 5% two or more races, and 21% White in Fall 2024.

Similarly, Saddleback College (SC) serves around 25,789 students, with demographics showing 12% Asian, 2% Black/African-American, 29% Hispanic/Latino, 5% two or more races, and 47% White in Fall 2024.

These numbers underscore the importance of our commitment to eliminating equity gaps across all student demographics through implementing dynamic, student-centered practices and policies. To support the academic and career success of our diverse student body, we seek a candidate who will actively contribute to our mission of inclusivity and support. The ideal candidate's values will align with SOCCCD’s goals for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) and Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO).

jobs.title: Project Coordinator - Federal
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Jacobs is a leading design firm in the Government, Commercial, Healthcare, Data Center and University sectors. We provide award winning architectural and engineering services in all phases of building design and construction. Our collaborative approach allows us to successfully deliver fully integrated professional services for a broad range of clients and project types worldwide.

At Jacobs, we help prepare people for new opportunities and challenges. With positions at every level, openings in multiple disciplines, expertise in a range of markets and offices around the globe, we create an environment where you can learn, grow, and thrive. From our competitive benefits program to our Health and Safety initiative of Beyond Zero workplace injuries, we believe that you'll find a flourishing career here at Jacobs.

Position Summary

The Project Coordinator serves as an integral partner to our Project Managers, helping drive the day-to-day execution and coordination of projects from initiation through closeout. Reporting to the Administration/Coordination Group Leader, this highly collaborative role goes beyond traditional administrative support by taking ownership of project coordination activities, anticipating project needs, proactively resolving issues, and helping keep projects organized and on schedule. This is far more than a traditional administrative support role. Successful Project Coordinators become trusted business partners who help Project Managers increase capacity, improve project execution, and deliver exceptional client service.

Working closely with Project Managers, technical teams, clients, and project stakeholders, the Project Coordinator develops an understanding of each Project Manager’s workflow, communication style, and project priorities. As Project Coordinators gain experience and build trusted partnerships with their Project Managers, they assume increasing responsibility throughout the project lifecycle, becoming an extension of the Project Manager and creating the capacity for Project Managers to focus on technical leadership, client relationships, and strategic project delivery.

In this role you will join a dedicated professional team working to make a difference for our Federal Government Clients to

Partner proactively with Project Managers and technical teams to coordinate project activities and support fast-paced, successful project delivery.
Manage electronic and physical project documentation, including filing, document control, scanning, tracking, distribution, and record management.
Coordinate project meetings by scheduling, preparing agendas, capturing action items, and following up on outstanding tasks.
Manage Outlook calendars, coordinate travel, and organize meetings with internal teams, clients, and project stakeholders.
Review, coordinate, and assist with processing project documentation, including submittals, invoices, and other project related administrative workflows.
Coordinate subcontractor documentation and assist with project setup, closeout, and ongoing project administration.
Monitor project schedules, milestones, action items, and deliverables to help ensure projects remain organized and on track.
Communicate professionally with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and integral project teams while serving as a trusted point of coordination/contact.
Manage office supplies, equipment, shipping, printing, and other operational support activities as needed.
Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements, including itineraries, and logistical planning
Research local conditions and provide logistical support for domestic and international project activities.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

Successful Project Coordinators are trusted partners who become an extension of their Project Managers. They proactively anticipate needs, adapt to each Project Manager’s work style, and continuously expand their project knowledge to assume greater responsibility over time. Rather than simply completing assigned tasks, they take ownership of project coordination activities, solve problems before they become obstacles, and contribute directly to the successful delivery of projects while creating additional capacity for Project Managers to focus on strategic and technical leadership.

Here's what you'll need

United States Citizenship
At least two years of college-level coursework or equivalent 
At least 3 years of project coordination experience in the architecture and engineering industry, preferred
Experience utilizing Specsintact and MasterSpec software preferred

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $79,500.00 to $110,800.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on July 31, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we’re focused on solving today’s environmental challenges by delivering innovative and sustainable solutions for our clients and communities. We are seeking an Entry-Level Field Technician to support our growing Colorado upstream oil and gas asset-retirement program and other environmental projects for government and private-sector clients.

Based out of the Loveland area, you'll support a variety of field and office tasks associated with environmental sampling, remediation system inspections, data collection, and site monitoring activities. Responsibilities include environmental sampling (groundwater, soil, soil vapor, or surface water), field documentation, subcontractor oversight, equipment troubleshooting, data entry, and coordination of field efforts. Approximately 85% of your time will be spent in the field, with the remaining time supporting project documentation and writing, logistics, and data management.

This position is ideal for a hands-on professional who enjoys fieldwork, problem-solving, and working collaboratively to support environmental compliance and remediation projects.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in environmental science, Environmental Engineering, Geology or related field.
0-2 years of environmental, engineering, geology, scientific, or related field experience
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate field documentation.
Ability to stand or walk for extended periods and lift and carry field equipment and sample coolers weighing up to approximately 40 pounds.
Ability to wear required personal protective equipment, including hardhats, safety glasses, gloves, safety-toe boots, and respiratory protection when required.
Willingness to travel throughout Colorado, work early field schedules, and occasionally stay overnight near project sites.
Commitment to working safely and protecting subcontractors, coworkers, clients, and the public
Strong communication, teamwork, and organizational skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
40-hour HAZWOPER certification or ability to obtain certification.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Experience using GPS units, mobile data-collection applications, field meters, or similar equipment
Experience completing field logs, inspection forms, or other detailed documentation
First Aid/CPR certification.
Experience with environmental sampling or field data collection.
General equipment maintenance experience.
Strong attention to detail and technical documentation skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. jobs.description:
Department Information

This position is only open to Colorado state residents.

NOTE:
This posting may fill more than one vacancy.

Thank you for your interest in working for the State of Colorado. Join us and find meaningful work in public service to our state and its residents, helping to make Colorado a great place to live and work in. Please watch the short video below for tips on applying. Apply for a job with the State of Colorado

To learn more about what happens after you apply for a position with the State of Colorado, please watch the short, informative video. What Happens After You Apply

Colorado for All Philosophy:
Colorado for All means working toward a Colorado where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. It means we support the basic human rights of our neighbors regardless of gender, race, ethnicity, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, education level, disability, socio-economic status, or any other visible or invisible identity.

The Department of Personnel & Administration (DPA)
is the foundation for dependable state government, leading with responsiveness, integrity, and teamwork. We provide services to other government agencies and all Coloradans by taking bold initiative toward a government with engaged employees, innovative solutions, and constructive partnerships.

DPA
provides a wide range of programs and services, from custodial & maintenance to financial and human resources support, which assist other state agencies in fulfilling their missions. At DPA, there are countless opportunities to contribute to meaningful work that supports and serves the people of Colorado. The wide variety of positions in DPA allow individuals to learn about state operations and provide for long-term career growth.

If your goal is to build a career that makes a difference and build greater public confidence in good government, consider joining the dedicated people of the State of Colorado; it's a chance to combine your expertise with public service. Our professionals strive to support state government and the residents of Colorado. Customer service is a key component for every position in state government as is the focus on ideas and ways to redesign the delivery of services in making state government more.

Good Government Starts Here!

Why We Want You

We want your expertise, positive energy, drive to succeed, and love of this great state as we work to elevate the expectations Coloradans have of their government.

What You'll Get From Us

In return for the skilled work you do, DPA provides a competitive compensation and benefits package to accompany employment opportunities. Please see the Benefits Overview video for details on the benefits offered to employees.

Description Of Job

The Equity Coordinator, Supplier Diversity is responsible for assisting small businesses and underutilized business groups through the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator program (State Equity in Procurement Help Desk) which includes the Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory/Apply and Verify program and the Colorado Resources Directory to include providing guidance with state processes and requirements in coordination with findings and recommendations from the Equity in Procurement State Disparity Report, Stakeholder Group Recommendation Report, Colorado Senate Bill 22-163 and C. R.S.

24-103-1104.

This position will perform the following functions: deliver real-time solicitation assistance to small businesses and underutilized business groups, collaborate with key stakeholders to maximize compliance and utilization of the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator, Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory, and the Colorado Resources Directory programs; develop program training and outreach to businesses; assist with the development of program practices, forms and templates to ensure that procedures are structured for effective consideration and participation of diverse businesses in all programs; and capture success measures and outcomes.

This position supports the Colorado Statewide Equity Office (SEO) by implementing processes and strategies to best support small and underutilized businesses through a solicitation/procurement help desk program and business verification and directory program.

A summary of the duties and responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Supplier Diversity Initiatives

Serve as the contact point for the Supplier Diversity Navigator, business directory, and resource directory and collaborates with key stakeholders to maximize compliance and utilization of the programs.
Conducts research and assists with improvements and integrations pertaining to the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator, the Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory, and the Colorado Resources Directory programs.
Helpdesk Support – Implement, course correct and review operational issues while logging helpdesk queries.
Ensure all queries are processed and compliant with DPA policies and procedures. Investigate/results, follow up and resolve open items.
Provide guidance and clarification on bids and contracts/solicitation assistance.
Carry out triaging and advise requesters to correct buying channels & respond to Procurement related inquiries.
Review and approve resource applications for the Colorado Resource Directory.
Provide Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory business directory guidance and assistance to small businesses and underutilized business groups.
This position will implement processes and strategies to best support small and diverse businesses through the Supplier Diversity program initiatives, as well as working closely and aligning with the State Purchasing and Contracts Office.

Vendor Assistance and Outreach:

Travel statewide to attend trade association meetings, vendor fairs and provide vendor training and outreach.
Promote doing business with the State at conferences where vendors are present by staffing resource tables, participating in webinars, and speaking in presentations about state procurement and Supplier Diversity Program resources.

Collaboration and Stakeholding:

This position will be required to attend all in-person monthly Statewide Equity Office team building micro-retreats/onsites.
Actively collaborate, participate in and support broader Statewide Equity Office initiatives and attend two annual Statewide Equity Office Community Engagement events of their choosing, outside of the additional Supplier Diversity Outreach events. These may be on the weekend.
Contribute recommendations from the Supplier Diversity program to cross-functional teams and projects aimed at advancing equity, diversity, and inclusion across state government and its services.
Collaborate with other SEO staff to align program goals and share best practices.
Collaborate with key stakeholders to develop targets and sourcing strategies designed to increase the utilization of diverse suppliers and small businesses.
Act as the administrator of the Supplier Diversity Statewide community of practice with support from the Manager.
Support your Statewide Community of Practice or others by potential meeting facilitation and guidance, meeting minute taking, event coordination, and consultation services.

Data Collection:

Leverages technology, digital tools, and data to contribute to program objectives and success measures, reporting outcomes to the Manager, Stakeholder Group, DPA Leadership, and other entities including the General Assembly, Governor’s Office, and others.
Conduct regular audits of directory listings to ensure contact information, service descriptions, and eligibility requirements remain accurate and active.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

A Human Resources Analyst will only review the work experience/job duties sections of the online job application to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for the position for which you are applying. Cover letters and resumes WILL NOT be accepted in lieu of the official State of Colorado online application , but may be attached. Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications to continue in the selection process for this position. Work experience and qualifications must be specifically documented on your online application. Do not use "see resume" or "see attached" statements on your application. Resumes WILL NOT be reviewed for minimum qualification screening. If it is determined that you meet the minimum qualifications, your application will also be used as part of the comparative analysis process to identify a top group for further consideration.

This position is advertised in line with the Governor’s executive order (Executive Order 2022 015 ) focused on skills-based hiring practices that focuses on the knowledge, skills, and abilities specific to the job and aligns the hiring process accordingly. Skills-based hiring reduces potential barriers for applicants and allows for reduced bias in the hiring process by providing a direct description of skills that are unique to the duties assigned to the position with a recognition that the applicant may have developed these skills through education, training or past experiences.

Residency Requirement

This posting is only open to residents of the State of Colorado at the time of submitting your application.

Class Code & Classification Description

H1A1XX

Program Coordinator

Minimum Qualifications

Experience Only:

At least six (6) years of relevant experience in procurement, small business administration, and/or administrative program support

Or

Education And Experience

A combination of related education and/or relevant experience in procurement, small business administration, and/or administrative program support equal to at least six (6) years.

The exceptional candidate
will possess the proven ability or accomplishment in the following preferred qualifications:

Previous State Service related to the work assigned to the position
Well versed in business acumen
Demonstrated ability to coordinate and manage EDI initiatives within a diverse and fluid organizational dynamic and manage goals and established parameters.
Demonstrated ability to develop and foster positive relationships with partners and stakeholders
Proven success in a collaborative, team-oriented environment
Ability to adapt approach, goals, and methods as necessary to achieve results and respond to changing priorities
Ability and desire to work in an environment that values, encourages, and supports all differences while aiming to advance equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) through daily work activities
Ability and desire to respectfully and actively engage with others with cultural identities different from your own
Awareness of biases, assumptions about human behavior, and values and a desire to strive for lifelong learning and growth

Conditions Of Employment

A pre-employment criminal background check will be conducted as part of the selection process.
Travel required: Attend all in-person monthly Statewide Equity Office team building micro-retreats and/or on-sites; attend trade association meetings, vendor fairs and provide vendor training and outreach statewide

Comparative Analysis Process

The comparative analysis process for this position may consist of a structured application review, an online assessment and a structured interview.

Appeal Rights

An applicant who has been removed from consideration during the selection or comparative analysis process, you may file an appeal with the State Personnel Board and/or request a review by the State Personnel Director. A standard appeal form is available on the State Personnel Board website, https://spb.colorado.gov/forms-and-filing . If you appeal, your appeal must be submitted in writing on the official appeal form, signed by you or your representative, and received at the following address within ten (10) days of your receipt of

jobs.description:
Job Description

GIS Technician I

Launch Your GIS Career with Pape-Dawson

Are you passionate about geospatial technology and eager to build your career with an industry-leading engineering and consulting firm? At Pape-Dawson, you'll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals on projects that help shape communities across the country. As a GIS Technician I, you'll gain hands-on experience with the latest GIS technologies while supporting impactful engineering, planning, environmental, and infrastructure projects.

Whether you're just beginning your GIS career or looking to grow your technical skills, you'll find a collaborative environment that encourages learning, mentorship, and professional development.

What You'll Do

Role

As a GIS Technician I, you'll support the development and maintenance of geospatial data, maps, and reporting products while working under the guidance of experienced GIS professionals. In this role, you will:

Create GIS data layers, maps, tables, reports, and other spatial deliverables using ESRI's ArcGIS suite and related applications.
Prepare, edit, and maintain geospatial datasets in accordance with project standards and quality requirements.
Collect, verify, organize, and manage spatial data from a variety of internal and external sources.
Perform basic spatial analysis and data updates using established GIS workflows and methodologies.
Support engineering, planning, and environmental teams by producing accurate mapping products and visualizations.
Collaborate with senior GIS staff while continuing to develop your technical knowledge and GIS best practices.
Contribute to a team culture focused on quality, innovation, and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

Associate degree in Geographic Information Systems or a related field (ESRI certification may be substituted for a degree).
Basic proficiency with ESRI ArcGIS software and related GIS applications.
Familiarity with surveys, legal descriptions, construction plans, aerial imagery, and orthophotography.
Understanding of cartographic principles, coordinate systems, map projections, scales, and spatial data management.
Ability to create clear, accurate maps and other geospatial deliverables.
Basic understanding of programming concepts and technical documentation.
Strong attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities.
Ability to work Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with occasional overtime as project needs require.

Why Join Pape-Dawson?

At Pape-Dawson, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We invest in our employees by providing opportunities to learn, grow, and build rewarding long-term careers. As one of the nation's leading engineering and consulting firms, you'll work on meaningful projects that improve infrastructure and strengthen communities while collaborating with talented professionals who are committed to excellence.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being, including:

Competitive compensation
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
401(k) with company matching
Paid time off and company holidays
Professional development, training, and career advancement opportunities
Collaborative, team-oriented culture with mentorship from experienced professionals
Opportunities to work on innovative, high-impact projects across multiple disciplines

If you're ready to build your GIS career with a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth, we'd love to hear from you.

This role does NOT offer sponsorship of any sort - including OPT VISAs, etc.

Energetics - CLEAResult Energy Sustainability Consulting
provides a full spectrum of clean energy consulting services to public and private sector clients. The Energetics team works with lead investors, innovators, and stakeholders to inform and expedite the development and market success of novel energy technologies, strategies and practices that deliver a sustainable future. Energetics was founded in 1979 and joined CLEAResult in 2024 as a division within CLEAResult's Energy Sustainability Services business.

Energetics is seeking an EV Charging Station Data Analyst.
The EV Charging Station Data Analyst will assist with the collection, processing, and analyzing of electric vehicle (EV) charging station data from numerous network service providers to generate a clean, aggregated dataset that drives interactive dashboards visualizing key statistics. Ideal candidates will be graduates with a degree in engineering, data science, or a technical field.

Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

Analyzing electric vehicle operational and charging session data
Creating data frameworks for automated data transfer
Conducting quality control on received data sets
Characterizing data by removing proprietary information
Adding cleansed data sets into the database for post-processing
Running utilization and other reports based on various attributes
Creating visually interesting tabular and graphical summaries
Deploying and running code on cloud computing platforms

Required Qualifications (includes Education, Experience, Competencies, Etc.)

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering, data science or a technical field from an accredited university
Data analysis software and programming experience (e.g., MS Azure, Python, Geographical Information System [GIS], Microsoft Power BI, Tableau)
Excellent communication skills (verbal, interpersonal, and written)
Interest in energy efficiency and clean energy with specific emphasis on transportation technologies such as: alternative fuels, vehicle electrification, and connected and autonomous vehicles
Excellent organization and time management skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office, with advanced Excel skills
Successful when working on self-managed tasks
Ability to work within a diverse team
Comfortable multitasking on time-sensitive tasks without diminished quality of work

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced data analytics and visualization (Python, R, Matlab) or GIS program use and results analysis
Degree in data science or related certifications
2-5 years of professional experience
Electric vehicle and charging station data collection and analysis
Database setup and management
Alternative fuels and transportation electrification familiarity
Data modeling & transformation
CI/CD workflow development
Cloud computing resource coordination & deployment

jobs.title: SURVEY TECHNICIAN
jobs.description:
At Nox Group, we are dedicated to humanizing construction as one of the fastest-growing industrial enterprises in the US. Nox Group owns and operates Corbins, RMCI, Nox Innovations, and Construction Labels, and our teams set the standard as industry leaders. As we continue to expand our reach nationwide, we seek people who are passionate about personal growth and eager to make a positive impact throughout the industries and communities we serve. We prioritize our people, our partners, and our relationships. Start your journey today and join our skilled team.

The Survey Technician is responsible for performing field survey, layout and data collection activities using Trimble RTS and GPS equipment to support construction operations. Working under the direction of the Survey Superintendent, this position ensures that layouts for equipment, conduit, trenching, and structural supports are accurate, documented, and aligned with project design intent. The Survey Technician plays a key role in maintaining project quality, accuracy, and efficiency while upholding all safety and company standards.

Responsibilities

Perform daily field layout activities using Trimble RTS and GPS equipment under the direction of the Survey Superintendent.
Set up, localize, and maintain survey equipment to project control points and verify calibration accuracy.
Execute layout tasks for:
Equipment pads and foundation locations
Trench routing, depth, and slope verification
Underground and overhead conduit pathways
Openings, racks, hangers, and other structural elements requiring layout precision
Field verification of correct installation prior to backfill

Collect and record as-built data for installed components.
Verify layout accuracy through field checks, checklist, and coordination with BIM/CAD models and the project VDC team.
Support the project team in transferring layout data between Trimble equipment and design models.
Assist in organizing survey data files, control points, and field documentation.
Report discrepancies or field challenges to the Survey Superintendent or project management for resolution.
Maintain cleanliness, calibration, and functionality of all Trimble RTS and GPS equipment and accessories.
Follow company and project safety procedures for survey and layout activities within active construction zones.
Participate in daily and weekly project meetings as needed to understand upcoming layout needs.
Provide feedback to improve layout workflows, documentation, and field coordination processes.

Qualifications

3-5 years of experience in survey, layout, or related construction field work preferred.
Working knowledge of Trimble RTS and GPS systems, data collection, and layout procedures; training provided as needed.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, civil plans, and basic BIM/CAD layouts.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.
Ability to walk or stand on job sites for extended periods of time and lift up to 50 lbs.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites as required.

Safety Level

This is a safety sensitive position, and all applicable policies including drug test and background check will apply.

The inherent responsibilities of your role may include physical working conditions. In order to safely and successfully perform job duties you must be able to:
Potentially lift up to 50 pounds
Potentially need to do repeated pushing, pulling, carrying, reaching (or working above shoulder), walking, standing, sitting, stooping, kneeling, bending, and climbing
Potentially operate a motor vehicle, crane, tractor, etc.

We reserve the right to continually monitor your ability to safely and successfully complete these inherent physical responsibilities and take action as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Americans with Disability Act (ADA)

jobs.title: Business Insights Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Welcome to Whataburger Careers!

Our Flavor — Why Whataburger

Whataburger isn’t just a fast-food burger chain it is where bold leadership starts — and where potential doesn’t just grow, it heats up. Whether you're leading the line or working behind the scenes, this is the place where opportunities stack up, and every day gives you a chance to Make a Difference.

Since 1950, we’ve invested in people who lead with integrity, Serve with Heart , and bring their best flavor to the team. We believe in working together, speaking up, having a little fun, and Winning as One — because great burgers (and great teams) start with the right ingredients. If you're ready — to learn, grow, impact, and Move Forward Boldly — we’ve got your back and your path cooked to perfection.

Your Recipe For Impact — What You’ll Do

As a Business Insights Data Analyst, you'll transform complex data into meaningful business insights that help drive smarter decisions across the organization. Through advanced analytics, reporting, and research, you'll uncover opportunities, identify trends, and deliver recommendations that improve business performance and support strategic growth.

In this role, you'll Make a Difference by turning data into actionable solutions that create measurable business value. You'll Serve with Heart by partnering with stakeholders across the organization to understand their needs and provide insights that help them succeed. You'll Win as One through cross-functional collaboration with teams across the business, building strong partnerships that fuel informed decision-making. And you'll Move Forward Boldly by leveraging analytics, innovation, and continuous improvement to uncover new opportunities and advance our data-driven culture.

Day-to-Day Ingredients — Responsibilities

As a Business Insights Data Analyst, you will:

Analyze complex data to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
Deliver actionable insights that support business decisions.
Extract, transform, validate, and manage data from multiple sources.
Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, and scorecards.
Perform ad hoc analyses to answer critical business questions.
Apply data mining and advanced analytical techniques to solve business challenges.
Design and measure tests, pilots, and business initiatives.
Partner with cross-functional teams to define reporting and analytics needs.
Present findings and recommendations to stakeholders and leadership.
Improve data quality, reporting efficiency, and data governance processes.
Support data warehouse, reporting, and analytics initiatives.

The Sauce — Pay & Perks

As a Business Insights Data Analyst, You Will Receive

Competitive Weekly Pay
Bonus Program that scales up to 2.5X payout potential based on company results
5 weeks PTO
Flex Weeks
Paid Corporate Holidays
Paid Parental Leave*
401(k) match $1/$1 up to 4%
Competitive Medical, Dental and Vision Benefits*
Short-term and Long-term Disability Benefits*
Opportunities for Career Development and Growth
Whataburger Family Foundation - Scholarship Program (dependents eligible) and Hardship Grant Assistance
Discounted Meals for You and a Guest
Wireless Service Discounts
Computer & Software Discounts
Fitness / Gym Discounts
Awards and recognition for all you do
Retirement Celebration Program

What You Bring To The Table — Required Experience

As a Business Insights Data Analyst, you must have:

Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Finance, Data Analytics, or a related quantitative field; or equivalent work experience.
Experience analyzing complex datasets and translating results into business recommendations.
Experience writing and optimizing SQL queries.
Experience with reporting, analytics, and data visualization tools.
Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to communicate complex findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience managing multiple projects and competing priorities.
Strong stakeholder partnership and collaboration skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and other business productivity tools.

Extra Toppings — Desired Experience

As a Business Insights Data Analyst, we prefer you to have:

Advanced degree in a quantitative discipline.
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization tools.
Experience with data modeling, ETL processes, and data warehousing.
Experience with Python, R, or other analytics programming languages.
Experience with machine learning or predictive analytics techniques.
Experience with web, digital, or customer analytics.
Experience building automated reporting solutions.
Experience supporting enterprise-scale analytics initiatives.
Restaurant, retail, hospitality, or consumer-facing industry experience.
Knowledge of cloud-based data and analytics platforms.

Where & How You’ll Work

This role is based at the San Antonio Home Office, working on‑site Monday through Thursday with remote flexibility on Fridays. In this role, you’ll have strong collaboration with leadership, across cross-functional teams, and with external partners to align capabilities with restaurant realities. The work environment is fast‑paced and requires sound judgment, strategic thinking, and strong collaboration skills. Full‑time availability is required, with occasional extended hours based on business needs, along with occasional travel to properties, project sites, and external meetings. Candidates must reside within commuting distance of the San Antonio Home Office.

Help

Qualifications

In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specilized experience at or equivalent to the 13 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following:

Experience providing detailed environmental compliance reviews acquired through extensive experience in technical evaluations, program planning, program management, and program administration concerned with the resolution of complex, technically difficult environmental problems often within the national public realm of debate.

Community Planning Series 0020

Education

A BASIC EDUCATION REQUIREMENT FOR THIS POSITION MUST BE MET AT TIME OF APPLICATION.

A transcript must be submitted with your application in order to verify the basic education requirements for this position. See Required Documents for additional information.

Applicants must meet the following Basic Requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual:

0020

Degree: community planning; or related field such as urban affairs, architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, sociology, geography, economics, political science, or public administration that included at least 12 semester hours in the planning process, socioeconomic and physical elements of planning, urban and regional economic analysis, and development finance.

Note: Applicants with degrees in related fields, such as those listed above, who do not have the 12 semester hours of specified course work must have had at least 1 year of work experience in community planning acquired under the supervision and guidance of a community planner.

OR

Combination of education and experience: courses equivalent to a major in one of the above disciplines, or a combination of related courses totaling at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the above disciplines of which at least 12 semester hours were in the planning process, and socioeconomic and physical elements of planning, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

0401

Degree: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR
Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

0819

Degree: Engineering. To be acceptable, the program must: (1) lead to a bachelor's degree in a school of engineering with at least one program accredited by ABET; or (2) include differential and integral calculus and courses (more advanced than first-year physics and chemistry) in five of the following seven areas of engineering science or physics: (a) statics, dynamics; (b) strength of materials (stress-strain relationships); (c) fluid mechanics, hydraulics; (d) thermodynamics; (e) electrical fields and circuits; (f) nature and properties of materials (relating particle and aggregate structure to properties); and (g) any other comparable area of fundamental engineering science or physics, such as optics, heat transfer, soil mechanics, or electronics. OR
Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. The adequacy of such background must be demonstrated by one of the following: 1. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.)

1301

Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR
Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

POSITION SPECIFICS

The Department of Ecosystem Science and Management
and the Department of Animal Science
at The Pennsylvania State University
are seeking a highly organized and motivated individual for a Research Technologist / Project and Outreach Coordinator
position. This professional staff position will support the research programs of Dr. Estelle Couradeau and Dr. Erika Ganda (50/50 split) by providing laboratory, project management, and outreach coordination support across multiple research projects. The position integrates laboratory operations, technical research support, project coordination, stakeholder engagement, and science communication activities.

The successful candidate will play a central role in ensuring the efficient operation of two research laboratories while helping coordinate project activities, outreach initiatives, and communication efforts. This position offers opportunities to develop expertise in laboratory management, microbiology and molecular biology research, project coordination, stakeholder engagement, science communication, and data management.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Manage laboratory purchasing, budget tracking, and supply ordering; maintain accurate records of expenditures and assist with financial documentation.
Support laboratory experiments and technical activities, including molecular and microbiological procedures such as DNA extraction, sample processing, and maintenance of laboratory protocols and standard operating procedures.
Maintain laboratory organization, inventory systems, laboratory safety records, equipment, and shared resources to ensure efficient laboratory operations.
Coordinate project activities, including scheduling meetings, tracking milestones and deliverables, maintaining project documentation, and facilitating communication among project participants.
Organize and support outreach and engagement activities with schools, community partners, collaborators, and research participants; assist with educational programming, curriculum development, and dissemination of project materials.
Support data management, data processing, and basic data analysis activities; assist in the preparation of reports, presentations, educational materials, and communication products.
Coordinate science communication activities, including multimedia content, public engagement events, podcasts, exhibits, and other outreach initiatives.
Maintain effective communication with laboratory personnel, project collaborators, external partners, and university staff to ensure projects remain on schedule and laboratory needs are met.

Required Qualifications

Strong organizational, project management, and time-management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common data management tools.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in microbiology, molecular biology, soil science, ecosystem science, environmental science, animal science, or related disciplines.
Experience with laboratory operations, inventory management, and laboratory safety practices.
Experience with project coordination, stakeholder engagement, education, outreach, or science communication.
Experience with data analysis software such as R and familiarity with GitHub or other collaborative data platforms.
Experience working with educational partners, agricultural stakeholders, community organizations, or research participants.

The position is expected to support long-term research and outreach activities across multiple projects and funding sources.

Minimum Education, Work Experience & Required Certifications

Bachelor's Degree No prior relevant work experience required; previous relevant work experience accepted in lieu of education. Required Certifications: None

Additional Information

Contact Dr. Couradeau (estelle@psu.edu) and Dr. Ganda (ganda@psu.edu ) for further questions. Applications will be reviewed immediately and are accepted until the position is filled.

Job Description

Mission Support and Test Services, LLC (MSTS) manages and operates the Nevada National Security Site (NNSS) for the U.S. National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). Our MISSION is to help ensure the security of the United States and its allies by providing high-hazard experimentation and incident response capabilities through operations, engineering, education, field, and integration services and by acting as environmental stewards to the Site’s Cold War legacy. Our VISION is to be the user site of choice for large-scale, high-hazard, national security experimentation, with premier facilities and capabilities below ground, on the ground, and in the air. (See NNSS.gov for our unique capabilities.) Our 2,750+ professional, craft, and support employees are called upon to innovate, collaborate, and deliver on some of the more difficult nuclear security challenges facing the world today.

MSTS offers our full-time employees highly competitive salaries and benefits packages including medical, dental, and vision; both a pension and a 401k; paid time off and 96 hours of paid holidays; relocation (if located more than 75 miles from work location); tuition assistance and reimbursement; and more.
MSTS is a limited liability company consisting of Honeywell International Inc. (Honeywell), Jacobs Engineering Group Inc. (Jacobs), and HII Nuclear Inc.

Responsibilities

This position will report to the Data and Diagnostics Manager. The Senior Geologist provides advanced geological expertise to support the collection, analysis, interpretation, and quality assurance of subsurface and operational Data.

Key Responsibilities

Function as Subject Matter Expert (SME) in the Data & Diagnostics Group, Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation Directorate.
Support programs and projects by planning and executing drilling projects, geologic modeling, geophysical well log evaluation and analysis, and subsurface geologic characterization, including underground geologic mapping and logging of drill core and cuttings.
Lead Geoscience teams on geology projects: Oversee well-site geologic support activities during drilling operations. Oversee surface and underground geologic mapping and sampling projects.
Oversee borehole geophysical logging operations, including work planning and field coordination. Assist in procurement and management of geophysical logging services subcontracts.
Draft technical reports, presentations, and publications. Present results of geologic/geophysical investigations in papers, project meetings, and conferences. Prepare and defend proposals for additional geologic work.
Assist in developing and managing project-specific relational databases of drill hole information, including construction data, geologic data, geophysical log data, and sample data.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a calculus-based technical (STEM) field plus at least 5 years relevant experience. Skill building experience must demonstrate either deeper technical specialization or additional cross-disciplinary knowledge. Graduate research experience may be recognized.
Bachelor's degree in a geosciences discipline preferred.
Master of Science or Doctorate degree in a geoscience discipline preferred.
Experience planning and leading drilling operations for exploration preferred, including experience with borehole design and familiarity with regulatory requirements.
Experience in borehole geophysical log interpretation preferred.
Experience in development/management of geologic framework models preferred. Experience with EarthVision or Datamine preferred.
Knowledge and experience in developing relational databases (e.g., AcQuire, FusionX) is preferred.
Working knowledge of Microsoft SharePoint, ArcGIS, and AutoDesk preferred.
Ability to execute work in a disciplined manner to demonstrate compliance with laws, codes, orders, and MSTS policies and procedures.
Ability to prioritize and schedule multiple activities in the most efficient manner and meet required deadlines.
Be team-oriented with good communication skills. Able to work closely with a diverse group of scientists and engineers.
Ability to builds teaming relationships with technical and other company organizations.
Executes work in a disciplined manner to demonstrate compliance with laws, codes, orders, and MSTS policies and procedures.
The primary work location will be at the Nevada National Security Site (located 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas, Nevada).
Work schedule will be 4/10s Monday through Thursday (subject to change).
Pre-placement physical examination, which includes a drug screen, is required. MSTS maintains a substance abuse policy that includes random drug testing.
Must possess a valid driver’s license.

jobs.description:
1163894_RR00121694 Job ID: 1163894_RR00121694

NYU Grossman School of Medicine is one of the nation's top-ranked medical schools. For 175 years, NYU Grossman School of Medicine has trained thousands of physicians and scientists who have helped to shape the course of medical history and enrich the lives of countless people. An integral part of NYU Langone Health, the Grossman School of Medicine at its core is committed to improving the human condition through medical education, scientific research, and direct patient care. At NYU Langone Health, equity and inclusion are fundamental values. We strive to be a place where our exceptionally talented faculty, staff, and students of all identities can thrive. We embrace inclusion and individual skills, ideas, and knowledge.

For more information, go to med.nyu.edu , and interact with us on LinkedIn , Glassdoor , Indeed , Facebook , X and Instagram .

Position Summary

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Data Analyst.

The Data Analyst will work directly with Dr. Horwitz, the Director of the Division of Healthcare Delivery Science and the Center for Healthcare Innovations and Delivery Science, as well as the Rapid RCT Lab. We are seeking a qualified Data Analyst to provide support for data management and analyses across the Rapid RCT portfolio of projects. The Data Analyst will be responsible for planning, designing, and implementing statistical analyses. A successful applicant will be able to work autonomously and comfortably in an academic medical center environment.

Job Responsibilities

Maintain existing data collection and analysis systems in support of the research protocol
Provide technical assistance to analysts and researchers in accessing and analyzing datasets, as needed
Create descriptive data summaries including visualizations and written descriptions of data findings for a wide range of audiences
Design and conduct analyses pertaining to data acquired through various data sources
Work with staff and others to facilitate automation of standard, recurrent data acquisition, management, analysis and reporting
Support the development of publications and conference presentations, including drafting academic and nonacademic publications, writing conference abstracts, conducting lit reviews and creating tables and other data visualizations for presentations
Under direct supervision by the Division Director and with the guidance of the team's lead biostatistician, conduct basic statistical analyses and present them to the team

Minimum Qualifications

To qualify you must have a Masters degree in health care economics, health care policy, applied statistics, data science, biostatistics or a Bachelors degree with relevant work experience; Strong quantitative skills and advanced programming skills in Stata, SAS, and/or R; At least 2 years of work experience and/or research experience in a relevant setting; Ability to select and apply appropriate statistical methods for collecting and summarizing varied data; Excellent organization, time management, and communication skills and the ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative research team

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of principles and methods of biostatistics; principles, theories, and procedures of epidemiology, including study design, statistical analysis, and causal inference; 2. Appropriate computer processing methods used to generate, organize and display statistical and research data; and standard English grammar, spelling, and usage; 3. Strong attention to detail; 4. Problem-solving and critical thinking skills; 5. Planning/organizational skills; 6. Personal motivation

Qualified candidates must be able to effectively communicate with all levels of the organization.

NYU Grossman School of Medicine provides its staff with far more than just a place to work. Rather, we are an institution you can be proud of, an institution where you'll feel good about devoting your time and your talents. At NYU Langone Health, we are committed to supporting our workforce and their loved ones with a comprehensive benefits and wellness package. Our offerings provide a robust support system for any stage of life, whether it's developing your career, starting a family, or saving for retirement. The support employees receive goes beyond a standard benefit offering, where employees have access to financial security benefits, a generous time-off program and employee resources groups for peer support. Additionally, all employees have access to our holistic employee wellness program, which focuses on seven key areas of well-being: physical, mental, nutritional, sleep, social, financial, and preventive care. The benefits and wellness package is designed to allow you to focus on what truly matters. Join us and experience the extensive resources and services designed to enhance your overall quality of life for you and your family.

NYU Grossman School of Medicine is an equal opportunity employer and committed to inclusion in all aspects of recruiting and employment. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration. We require applications to be completed online.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a Senior Data Analyst
with strong experience in healthcare and pharmacy analytics
to support data-driven initiatives focused on medication adherence, pharmacy quality, and value-based care performance. This role is ideal for a hands-on analyst who thrives working with complex healthcare datasets, develops impactful dashboards, and translates data into actionable insights for clinical, operational, and executive stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities

Analyze and integrate large-scale healthcare datasets, including medical and pharmacy claims, membership, provider, and utilization data.
Develop, optimize, and maintain complex SQL and SAS queries for recurring and ad hoc analyses.
Design, build, and maintain Tableau dashboards and performance reports for clinical, quality, and operational leadership.
Perform trend analysis, root cause investigations, and performance monitoring related to medication adherence, pharmacy quality measures, utilization, and care management initiatives.
Identify performance gaps, cost drivers, and opportunities for operational and clinical improvement.
Present analytical findings through clear, executive-level reporting and data storytelling.
Support ad hoc analytics projects and business initiatives as needed.
Collaborate with IT, data engineering, and business stakeholders to improve data integration, reporting, and analytics processes.
Ensure compliance with HIPAA, CMS, and other applicable regulatory reporting requirements.
Support initiatives related to value-based care, quality programs, and accreditation.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Healthcare Administration, Statistics, or a related field.
5+ years of hands-on experience using SQL and SAS in a production environment.
3–4+ years of Tableau dashboard development, including dashboard design, visualization, and data storytelling.
3–4+ years of healthcare analytics experience.
Direct experience working with pharmacy claims data and pharmacy analytics.
Experience within a health plan or managed care environment.
Hands-on experience with medication adherence and pharmacy quality measures (e.g., PDC, MPR, CMS Star Ratings).
Experience supporting value-based care analytics and quality improvement initiatives.
Proven ability to work with large, complex healthcare datasets.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Python for data analysis or automation.
Experience developing reports and dashboards using Power BI.

Working Conditions

This is a fully remote position.
Work is performed in a standard home office environment with no unusual physical demands or hazards.

The qualifications listed above are intended to represent the minimum education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities required to successfully perform the essential duties of this position.

basis. Nothing contained in this job description should be construed as creating an employment contract or guarantee of continued employment.
