About The Company

Stellantis is a leading global automotive manufacturer committed to innovation, sustainability, and delivering exceptional mobility solutions. With a diverse portfolio of iconic brands and a focus on cutting-edge technology, Stellantis strives to shape the future of transportation. The company fosters a dynamic and inclusive work environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and continuous growth. As a pioneer in the automotive industry, Stellantis is dedicated to creating value for its customers, employees, and stakeholders worldwide.

About The Role

The Data Analyst / Front‑End App Developer at Stellantis plays a vital role in transforming complex Purchasing data into accessible and actionable insights through the development of analytics and front‑end data applications. This position involves designing, building, and maintaining dashboards, reports, and interactive data tools that support strategic decision-making across the organization. Working closely with the Data & AI Product Owner, the incumbent ensures that data products meet business needs, adhere to standard design practices, and provide intuitive user experiences. The role requires a blend of technical expertise in data analysis and front-end development, along with a strong understanding of business processes related to purchasing operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, or a related field. A master’s degree is a plus.
Proven experience in data analysis, dashboard development, and front-end application design.
Strong proficiency in data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Experience with front-end technologies including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and frameworks like React or Angular.
Familiarity with data querying languages such as SQL and data management practices.
Knowledge of data validation, quality assurance, and troubleshooting techniques.
Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to translate business requirements into technical solutions.
Strong communication skills, capable of working collaboratively with cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain interactive dashboards, reports, and front-end data applications aligned with product requirements and business needs.
Implement user-friendly interfaces with filters, drill-downs, and interactive views to enhance data accessibility and usability.
Ensure the accuracy, clarity, and consistency of analytics outputs, aligning with organizational data definitions and standards.
Analyze Purchasing data to identify trends, anomalies, and actionable insights that support strategic initiatives.
Collaborate with Data Managers and the Product Owner to validate data accuracy and resolve discrepancies.
Support root-cause analysis by surfacing data patterns and anomalies to facilitate problem resolution.
Translate business requirements from the Product Owner into functional analytics deliverables and front-end features.
Participate in testing, validation, and deployment of data products to ensure quality and reliability.
Continuously seek opportunities for process improvements and automation to enhance data delivery and user experience.

Benefits

Stellantis offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and professional growth of its employees. This includes competitive salary packages, health and dental insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off. Employees have access to ongoing training and development programs, fostering continuous learning and career advancement. The company promotes a collaborative and inclusive culture, encouraging innovation and diversity. Additionally, Stellantis provides flexible work arrangements and wellness initiatives aimed at maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

Equal Opportunity

Stellantis is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic. We believe diversity drives innovation and are dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive and contribute to our shared success.

Confluence is seeking a seasoned GIS Specialist to support our environmental consulting projects across the Rocky Mountain region. Unlike many GIS roles that only “produce maps,” this position is central to our enterprise GIS program and the success of our projects. You will enforce internal GIS standards, validate and manage incoming datasets, standardize workflows, and maintain our ArcGIS Online infrastructure and spatial data resources to maintain and improve on critical data analysis and reporting needs. Your work will directly support field operations, regulatory compliance, and client deliverables by producing high-quality analysis, figures, and interactive maps.

The ideal candidate excels in Esri platforms, enforces data quality standards, and integrates drone-collected imagery with environmental data for client-ready results. This role combines data architecture and workflow automation with the production of professional maps and graphics that directly support environmental assessments, permitting, and project management.

Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and enforce standardized GIS templates, symbology, and workflows across company projects.

Develop quality assurance plans to validate and quality control incoming spatial datasets and outgoing deliverables to ensure compliance with regulatory, client, and company standards.

Maintain and enhance the company’s ArcGIS Online spatial database, including data organization, permissions, and quality control.

Produce high-quality maps, figures, dashboards, and spatial analyses to support environmental assessments, regulatory submittals, and client deliverables.

Design and deploy Survey123 forms, field maps, and mobile applications to support field data collection and monitoring activities.

Integrate drone-collected ortho-imagery with Global Positioning System (GPS)-referenced field data for sub-meter to sub-inch precision mapping.

Support data automation by developing workflows that link laboratory results with field sample locations and other project datasets.

Collaborate with scientists, project managers, and field crews to integrate spatial analysis into project planning, compliance documentation, and client presentations.

Provide training, support, and licensing management for staff using ArcGIS products.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Geography, GIS, Environmental Science, or related field.

3–7 years of professional GIS experience in environmental consulting, natural resources, or a related industry.

Demonstrated proficiency with Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated tools/platforms (Survey123, Field Maps, Dashboards).

Strong technical skills in geodatabase design, feature services, and data integration.

Solid grasp of projections, coordinate systems, datum transforms, spatial resolution, data accuracy, and Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC) principles.

Proficiency in data management and automation workflows (Python preferred).

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present spatial analysis to technical and non-technical audiences.

Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines.

Must pass a standard background check.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Colorado Energy & Carbon Management Commission (ECMC), Wyoming Oil & Gas Conservation Commission (WOGCC), and Bureau of Land Management (BLM) regulatory environments.

Experience with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), Clean Water Act (CWA), and other applicable federal and state regulatory frameworks.

Professional GIS certification (GISP) or progress toward certification.

Experience with oil and gas projects, particularly upstream and midstream operations.

Demonstrated knowledge of spatial data standards and formats required by regulatory agencies.

Experience producing GIS deliverables for permitting, compliance reporting, or regulatory submittals.

Advanced Python scripting for automation and geoprocessing.

Experience with remote sensing and photogrammetry (drone/Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) data).

Proficiency with ArcGIS Online administration and web mapping services.

Background in environmental fieldwork, GPS data collection, or survey support.

At Jacobs, we help prepare people for new opportunities and challenges. Position Summary

The Project Coordinator serves as an integral partner to our Project Managers, helping drive the day-to-day execution and coordination of projects from initiation through closeout. Reporting to the Administration/Coordination Group Leader, this highly collaborative role goes beyond traditional administrative support by taking ownership of project coordination activities, anticipating project needs, proactively resolving issues, and helping keep projects organized and on schedule. This is far more than a traditional administrative support role. Successful Project Coordinators become trusted business partners who help Project Managers increase capacity, improve project execution, and deliver exceptional client service.

Working closely with Project Managers, technical teams, clients, and project stakeholders, the Project Coordinator develops an understanding of each Project Manager’s workflow, communication style, and project priorities. As Project Coordinators gain experience and build trusted partnerships with their Project Managers, they assume increasing responsibility throughout the project lifecycle, becoming an extension of the Project Manager and creating the capacity for Project Managers to focus on technical leadership, client relationships, and strategic project delivery.

In this role you will join a dedicated professional team working to make a difference for our Federal Government Clients to

Partner proactively with Project Managers and technical teams to coordinate project activities and support fast-paced, successful project delivery.
Manage electronic and physical project documentation, including filing, document control, scanning, tracking, distribution, and record management.
Coordinate project meetings by scheduling, preparing agendas, capturing action items, and following up on outstanding tasks.
Manage Outlook calendars, coordinate travel, and organize meetings with internal teams, clients, and project stakeholders.
Review, coordinate, and assist with processing project documentation, including submittals, invoices, and other project related administrative workflows.
Coordinate subcontractor documentation and assist with project setup, closeout, and ongoing project administration.
Monitor project schedules, milestones, action items, and deliverables to help ensure projects remain organized and on track.
Communicate professionally with clients, consultants, subcontractors, and integral project teams while serving as a trusted point of coordination/contact.
Manage office supplies, equipment, shipping, printing, and other operational support activities as needed.
Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements, including itineraries, and logistical planning
Research local conditions and provide logistical support for domestic and international project activities.

What Success Looks Like in This Role

Successful Project Coordinators are trusted partners who become an extension of their Project Managers. They proactively anticipate needs, adapt to each Project Manager’s work style, and continuously expand their project knowledge to assume greater responsibility over time. Rather than simply completing assigned tasks, they take ownership of project coordination activities, solve problems before they become obstacles, and contribute directly to the successful delivery of projects while creating additional capacity for Project Managers to focus on strategic and technical leadership.

What You'll Get From Us

In return for the skilled work you do, DPA provides a competitive compensation and benefits package to accompany employment opportunities. Please see the Benefits Overview video for details on the benefits offered to employees.

Description Of Job

The Equity Coordinator, Supplier Diversity is responsible for assisting small businesses and underutilized business groups through the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator program (State Equity in Procurement Help Desk) which includes the Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory/Apply and Verify program and the Colorado Resources Directory to include providing guidance with state processes and requirements in coordination with findings and recommendations from the Equity in Procurement State Disparity Report, Stakeholder Group Recommendation Report, Colorado Senate Bill 22-163 and C. R.S.

24-103-1104.

This position will perform the following functions: deliver real-time solicitation assistance to small businesses and underutilized business groups, collaborate with key stakeholders to maximize compliance and utilization of the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator, Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory, and the Colorado Resources Directory programs; develop program training and outreach to businesses; assist with the development of program practices, forms and templates to ensure that procedures are structured for effective consideration and participation of diverse businesses in all programs; and capture success measures and outcomes.

This position supports the Colorado Statewide Equity Office (SEO) by implementing processes and strategies to best support small and underutilized businesses through a solicitation/procurement help desk program and business verification and directory program.

A summary of the duties and responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:

Supplier Diversity Initiatives

Serve as the contact point for the Supplier Diversity Navigator, business directory, and resource directory and collaborates with key stakeholders to maximize compliance and utilization of the programs.
Conducts research and assists with improvements and integrations pertaining to the Colorado Supplier Diversity Navigator, the Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory, and the Colorado Resources Directory programs.
Helpdesk Support – Implement, course correct and review operational issues while logging helpdesk queries.
Ensure all queries are processed and compliant with DPA policies and procedures. Investigate/results, follow up and resolve open items.
Provide guidance and clarification on bids and contracts/solicitation assistance.
Carry out triaging and advise requesters to correct buying channels & respond to Procurement related inquiries.
Review and approve resource applications for the Colorado Resource Directory.
Provide Colorado Supplier Diversity Directory business directory guidance and assistance to small businesses and underutilized business groups.
This position will implement processes and strategies to best support small and diverse businesses through the Supplier Diversity program initiatives, as well as working closely and aligning with the State Purchasing and Contracts Office.

Vendor Assistance and Outreach:

Travel statewide to attend trade association meetings, vendor fairs and provide vendor training and outreach.
Promote doing business with the State at conferences where vendors are present by staffing resource tables, participating in webinars, and speaking in presentations about state procurement and Supplier Diversity Program resources.

Collaboration and Stakeholding:

This position will be required to attend all in-person monthly Statewide Equity Office team building micro-retreats/onsites.
Actively collaborate, participate in and support broader Statewide Equity Office initiatives and attend two annual Statewide Equity Office Community Engagement events of their choosing, outside of the additional Supplier Diversity Outreach events. These may be on the weekend.
Contribute recommendations from the Supplier Diversity program to cross-functional teams and projects aimed at advancing equity, diversity, and inclusion across state government and its services.
Collaborate with other SEO staff to align program goals and share best practices.
Collaborate with key stakeholders to develop targets and sourcing strategies designed to increase the utilization of diverse suppliers and small businesses.
Act as the administrator of the Supplier Diversity Statewide community of practice with support from the Manager.
Support your Statewide Community of Practice or others by potential meeting facilitation and guidance, meeting minute taking, event coordination, and consultation services.

Data Collection:

Leverages technology, digital tools, and data to contribute to program objectives and success measures, reporting outcomes to the Manager, Stakeholder Group, DPA Leadership, and other entities including the General Assembly, Governor’s Office, and others.
Conduct regular audits of directory listings to ensure contact information, service descriptions, and eligibility requirements remain accurate and active.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

A Human Resources Analyst will only review the work experience/job duties sections of the online job application to determine whether you meet the minimum qualifications for the position for which you are applying. Cover letters and resumes WILL NOT be accepted in lieu of the official State of Colorado online application , but may be attached. Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications to continue in the selection process for this position. Work experience and qualifications must be specifically documented on your online application. Do not use "see resume" or "see attached" statements on your application. Resumes WILL NOT be reviewed for minimum qualification screening. If it is determined that you meet the minimum qualifications, your application will also be used as part of the comparative analysis process to identify a top group for further consideration.

This position is advertised in line with the Governor’s executive order (Executive Order 2022 015 ) focused on skills-based hiring practices that focuses on the knowledge, skills, and abilities specific to the job and aligns the hiring process accordingly. Skills-based hiring reduces potential barriers for applicants and allows for reduced bias in the hiring process by providing a direct description of skills that are unique to the duties assigned to the position with a recognition that the applicant may have developed these skills through education, training or past experiences.

new_jobs.title: GIS Technician
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

GIS Technician I

Launch Your GIS Career with Pape-Dawson

Are you passionate about geospatial technology and eager to build your career with an industry-leading engineering and consulting firm? At Pape-Dawson, you'll have the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals on projects that help shape communities across the country. As a GIS Technician I, you'll gain hands-on experience with the latest GIS technologies while supporting impactful engineering, planning, environmental, and infrastructure projects.

Whether you're just beginning your GIS career or looking to grow your technical skills, you'll find a collaborative environment that encourages learning, mentorship, and professional development.

What You'll Do

Role

As a GIS Technician I, you'll support the development and maintenance of geospatial data, maps, and reporting products while working under the guidance of experienced GIS professionals. In this role, you will:

Create GIS data layers, maps, tables, reports, and other spatial deliverables using ESRI's ArcGIS suite and related applications.
Prepare, edit, and maintain geospatial datasets in accordance with project standards and quality requirements.
Collect, verify, organize, and manage spatial data from a variety of internal and external sources.
Perform basic spatial analysis and data updates using established GIS workflows and methodologies.
Support engineering, planning, and environmental teams by producing accurate mapping products and visualizations.
Collaborate with senior GIS staff while continuing to develop your technical knowledge and GIS best practices.
Contribute to a team culture focused on quality, innovation, and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

Associate degree in Geographic Information Systems or a related field (ESRI certification may be substituted for a degree).
Basic proficiency with ESRI ArcGIS software and related GIS applications.
Familiarity with surveys, legal descriptions, construction plans, aerial imagery, and orthophotography.
Understanding of cartographic principles, coordinate systems, map projections, scales, and spatial data management.
Ability to create clear, accurate maps and other geospatial deliverables.
Basic understanding of programming concepts and technical documentation.
Strong attention to detail, organization, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment while managing multiple priorities.
Ability to work Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., with occasional overtime as project needs require.

Why Join Pape-Dawson?

At Pape-Dawson, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We invest in our employees by providing opportunities to learn, grow, and build rewarding long-term careers. As one of the nation's leading engineering and consulting firms, you'll work on meaningful projects that improve infrastructure and strengthen communities while collaborating with talented professionals who are committed to excellence.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being, including:

Competitive compensation
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
401(k) with company matching
Paid time off and company holidays
Professional development, training, and career advancement opportunities
Collaborative, team-oriented culture with mentorship from experienced professionals
Opportunities to work on innovative, high-impact projects across multiple disciplines

If you're ready to build your GIS career with a company that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth, we'd love to hear from you.

EEO Statement

All qualified applicants for Pape-Dawson Engineers will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Paid Volunteer Time: giving back to our communities is important to us
Employee Recognition Program – convert your recognition points into gift cards
Employee Assistance Program – offers benefits to help you manage daily responsibilities
Access to on-demand training courses to advance further in your career

Job Description

Please Note - we have a strong preference for candidates who are within a drivable distance to Columbia, MD for ~weekly team meetings. Candidates outside of MD must have an exceptional fit to the role for consideration.

This role does NOT offer sponsorship of any sort - including OPT VISAs, etc.

Energetics - CLEAResult Energy Sustainability Consulting
provides a full spectrum of clean energy consulting services to public and private sector clients. The Energetics team works with lead investors, innovators, and stakeholders to inform and expedite the development and market success of novel energy technologies, strategies and practices that deliver a sustainable future. Energetics was founded in 1979 and joined CLEAResult in 2024 as a division within CLEAResult's Energy Sustainability Services business.

Energetics is seeking an EV Charging Station Data Analyst.
The EV Charging Station Data Analyst will assist with the collection, processing, and analyzing of electric vehicle (EV) charging station data from numerous network service providers to generate a clean, aggregated dataset that drives interactive dashboards visualizing key statistics. Ideal candidates will be graduates with a degree in engineering, data science, or a technical field.

Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

Analyzing electric vehicle operational and charging session data
Creating data frameworks for automated data transfer
Conducting quality control on received data sets
Characterizing data by removing proprietary information
Adding cleansed data sets into the database for post-processing
Running utilization and other reports based on various attributes
Creating visually interesting tabular and graphical summaries
Deploying and running code on cloud computing platforms

Required Qualifications (includes Education, Experience, Competencies, Etc.)

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering, data science or a technical field from an accredited university
Data analysis software and programming experience (e.g., MS Azure, Python, Geographical Information System [GIS], Microsoft Power BI, Tableau)
Excellent communication skills (verbal, interpersonal, and written)
Interest in energy efficiency and clean energy with specific emphasis on transportation technologies such as: alternative fuels, vehicle electrification, and connected and autonomous vehicles
Excellent organization and time management skills
Proficient in Microsoft Office, with advanced Excel skills
Successful when working on self-managed tasks
Ability to work within a diverse team
Comfortable multitasking on time-sensitive tasks without diminished quality of work

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced data analytics and visualization (Python, R, Matlab) or GIS program use and results analysis
Degree in data science or related certifications
2-5 years of professional experience
Electric vehicle and charging station data collection and analysis
Database setup and management
Alternative fuels and transportation electrification familiarity
Data modeling & transformation
CI/CD workflow development
Cloud computing resource coordination & deployment

Target Compensation

$61,100 - 70,000

DOT Requirements

If applicable, meet all DOT qualification requirements and comply with all applicable federal, state, and local transportation regulations.

Compensation Range

$61,100.00 - $78,000.00

Currency

USD

Type

Salary

Any offered salary is determined based on internal equity, internal salary ranges, market data/ranges, applicant’s skills and prior relevant experience, certain degrees and certifications (e.g. JD/technology), for example.

CLEAResult will not provide sponsorship or support for immigration status or work authorization including for international students. Applicants must be authorized to work in the country where the position is located without the need for employer sponsorship or support. Successful hires must pass pre-employment checks.

Mentor and guide junior team members

5 years of experience

Understanding GIS Business Solution for utilities

new_jobs.title: Procurement Process & Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match.

Role Summary

Are you passionate about data, continuous improvement, and digital transformation? Join us in a role where your analytical skills, ideas, and collaborative spirit can make a real impact. We are looking for someone who enjoys developing smart solutions through technology and automation and who is motivated to help others grow along the way. If you have a background in Information Systems or Supply Chain, we would love to hear from you.

About The Position

As a Procurement Process & Data Analyst, you will play an important role in connecting business needs with information technology to deliver meaningful and effective solutions. Working closely with cross-functional stakeholders, you will help identify procurement requirements, map and improve internal processes, and turn data and insights into digital solutions that create value for the business. In this role, you will also contribute to a collaborative environment by sharing knowledge, supporting colleagues, and helping drive continuous development across the team.

Location:
This is an onsite position based in Shippensburg, PA, USA.

What You Will Do

Analyze procurement business requirements and propose effective functional and digital solutions.
Create data analyses, dashboards, and visualizations to support data-driven decisions.
Map, review, and improve procurement processes and systems end to end.
Develop and maintain business intelligence tools and applications, mainly using Power BI, Qlik Sense, and Power Apps.
Use artificial intelligence tools to support smarter ways of working and help strengthen data literacy across the team.
Lead improvement initiatives from definition through implementation, ensuring stakeholder alignment and delivery of expected outcomes.
Apply data analytics and data quality principles to improve process performance and business insights.
Develop automation routines and workflows, mainly using Power Automate, to improve efficiency and data integrity.
Support process measurement and adherence to defined methods, tools, and ways of working.
Help ensure procurement routines support relevant business, regulatory, and compliance requirements.
Provide training and create work instructions for purchasing and supply chain professionals.
Support strategic regional activities related to quality, sustainability, capacity, and cost.
Represent the team and region in cross-functional and global forums.

Who are you?

Experience providing detailed environmental compliance reviews acquired through extensive experience in technical evaluations, program planning, program management, and program administration concerned with the resolution of complex, technically difficult environmental problems often within the national public realm of debate.

Education

A BASIC EDUCATION REQUIREMENT FOR THIS POSITION MUST BE MET AT TIME OF APPLICATION.

Applicants must meet the following Basic Requirements of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Standards Manual:

0020

Degree: community planning; or related field such as urban affairs, architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, sociology, geography, economics, political science, or public administration that included at least 12 semester hours in the planning process, socioeconomic and physical elements of planning, urban and regional economic analysis, and development finance.

OR

Combination of education and experience: courses equivalent to a major in one of the above disciplines, or a combination of related courses totaling at least 24 semester hours in any combination of the above disciplines of which at least 12 semester hours were in the planning process, and socioeconomic and physical elements of planning, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

0401

Degree: biological sciences, agriculture, natural resource management, chemistry, or related disciplines appropriate to the position. OR
Combination of education and experience: Courses equivalent to a major, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

0819

Degree: Engineering. Combination of education and experience -- college-level education, training, and/or technical experience that furnished (1) a thorough knowledge of the physical and mathematical sciences underlying engineering, and (2) a good understanding, both theoretical and practical, of the engineering sciences and techniques and their applications to one of the branches of engineering. Professional registration or licensure -- Current registration as an Engineer Intern (EI), Engineer in Training (EIT)1, or licensure as a Professional Engineer (PE) by any State, the District of Columbia, Guam, or Puerto Rico. Absent other means of qualifying under this standard, those applicants who achieved such registration by means other than written test (e.g., State grandfather or eminence provisions) are eligible only for positions that are within or closely related to the specialty field of their registration. For example, an applicant who attains registration through a State Board's eminence provision as a manufacturing engineer typically would be rated eligible only for manufacturing engineering positions. 2. Written Test -- Evidence of having successfully passed the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE)2 examination or any other written test required for professional registration by an engineering licensure board in the various States, the District of Columbia, Guam, and Puerto Rico. 3. Specified academic courses -- Successful completion of at least 60 semester hours of courses in the physical, mathematical, and engineering sciences and that included the courses specified in the basic requirements under paragraph A. The courses must be fully acceptable toward meeting the requirements of an engineering program as described in paragraph A. 4. Related curriculum -- Successful completion of a curriculum leading to a bachelor's degree in an appropriate scientific field, e.g., engineering technology, physics, chemistry, architecture, computer science, mathematics, hydrology, or geology, may be accepted in lieu of a bachelor's degree in engineering, provided the applicant has had at least 1 year of professional engineering experience acquired under professional engineering supervision and guidance. Ordinarily there should be either an established plan of intensive training to develop professional engineering competence, or several years of prior professional engineering-type experience, e.g., in interdisciplinary positions. (The above examples of related curricula are not all inclusive.)

1301

Degree: physical science, engineering, or mathematics that included 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science such as mechanics, dynamics, properties of materials, and electronics. OR
Combination of education and experience -- education equivalent to one of the majors shown in A above that included at least 24 semester hours in physical science and/or related engineering science, plus appropriate experience or additional education.

new_jobs.title: Senior Geologist (Senior Scientist)
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Mission Support and Test Services, LLC (MSTS) manages and operates the Nevada National Security Site (NNSS) for the U.S. National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). Our MISSION is to help ensure the security of the United States and its allies by providing high-hazard experimentation and incident response capabilities through operations, engineering, education, field, and integration services and by acting as environmental stewards to the Site’s Cold War legacy. Our VISION is to be the user site of choice for large-scale, high-hazard, national security experimentation, with premier facilities and capabilities below ground, on the ground, and in the air. (See NNSS.gov for our unique capabilities.) Our 2,750+ professional, craft, and support employees are called upon to innovate, collaborate, and deliver on some of the more difficult nuclear security challenges facing the world today.

MSTS offers our full-time employees highly competitive salaries and benefits packages including medical, dental, and vision; both a pension and a 401k; paid time off and 96 hours of paid holidays; relocation (if located more than 75 miles from work location); tuition assistance and reimbursement; and more.
MSTS is a limited liability company consisting of Honeywell International Inc. (Honeywell), Jacobs Engineering Group Inc. (Jacobs), and HII Nuclear Inc.

Responsibilities

This position will report to the Data and Diagnostics Manager. The Senior Geologist provides advanced geological expertise to support the collection, analysis, interpretation, and quality assurance of subsurface and operational Data.

Key Responsibilities

Function as Subject Matter Expert (SME) in the Data & Diagnostics Group, Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation Directorate.
Support programs and projects by planning and executing drilling projects, geologic modeling, geophysical well log evaluation and analysis, and subsurface geologic characterization, including underground geologic mapping and logging of drill core and cuttings.
Lead Geoscience teams on geology projects: Oversee well-site geologic support activities during drilling operations. Oversee surface and underground geologic mapping and sampling projects.
Oversee borehole geophysical logging operations, including work planning and field coordination. Assist in procurement and management of geophysical logging services subcontracts.
Draft technical reports, presentations, and publications. Present results of geologic/geophysical investigations in papers, project meetings, and conferences. Prepare and defend proposals for additional geologic work.
Assist in developing and managing project-specific relational databases of drill hole information, including construction data, geologic data, geophysical log data, and sample data.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a calculus-based technical (STEM) field plus at least 5 years relevant experience. Skill building experience must demonstrate either deeper technical specialization or additional cross-disciplinary knowledge. Graduate research experience may be recognized.
Bachelor's degree in a geosciences discipline preferred.
Master of Science or Doctorate degree in a geoscience discipline preferred.
Experience planning and leading drilling operations for exploration preferred, including experience with borehole design and familiarity with regulatory requirements.
Experience in borehole geophysical log interpretation preferred.
Experience in development/management of geologic framework models preferred. Experience with EarthVision or Datamine preferred.
Knowledge and experience in developing relational databases (e.g., AcQuire, FusionX) is preferred.
Working knowledge of Microsoft SharePoint, ArcGIS, and AutoDesk preferred.
Ability to execute work in a disciplined manner to demonstrate compliance with laws, codes, orders, and MSTS policies and procedures.
Ability to prioritize and schedule multiple activities in the most efficient manner and meet required deadlines.
Be team-oriented with good communication skills. Able to work closely with a diverse group of scientists and engineers.
Ability to builds teaming relationships with technical and other company organizations.
Executes work in a disciplined manner to demonstrate compliance with laws, codes, orders, and MSTS policies and procedures.
The primary work location will be at the Nevada National Security Site (located 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas, Nevada).
Work schedule will be 4/10s Monday through Thursday (subject to change).
Pre-placement physical examination, which includes a drug screen, is required. MSTS maintains a substance abuse policy that includes random drug testing.
Must possess a valid driver’s license.

MSTS is required by DOE directive to conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Applicants offered employment with MSTS are also subject to a federal background investigation to meet the requirements for access to classified information or matter if the duties of the position require a DOE security clearance. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause a clearance to be denied or terminated by DOE, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment. In addition, Applicants for employment must be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship, at least 18 years of age. Reference DOE Order 472.2 , “Personnel Security”. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Department of Energy Q Clearance
(position will be cleared to this level). Reviews and tests for the absence of any illegal drug as defined in 10 CFR Part 707.4 , “Workplace Substance Abuse Programs at DOE Sites,” will be conducted. Applicant selected will be subject to a Federal background investigation, required to participate in subsequent reinvestigations, and must meet the eligibility requirements for access to classified matter. Successful completion of a counterintelligence evaluation, which may include a counterintelligence-scope polygraph examination, may also be required. Reference 10 CFR Part 709 , “Counterintelligence Evaluation Program.”

MSTS is a background screening, drug-free workplace.

We prioritize our people, our partners, and our relationships. Start your journey today and join our skilled team.

The Survey Technician is responsible for performing field survey, layout and data collection activities using Trimble RTS and GPS equipment to support construction operations. Working under the direction of the Survey Superintendent, this position ensures that layouts for equipment, conduit, trenching, and structural supports are accurate, documented, and aligned with project design intent. The Survey Technician plays a key role in maintaining project quality, accuracy, and efficiency while upholding all safety and company standards.

Responsibilities

Perform daily field layout activities using Trimble RTS and GPS equipment under the direction of the Survey Superintendent.
Set up, localize, and maintain survey equipment to project control points and verify calibration accuracy.
Execute layout tasks for:
Equipment pads and foundation locations
Trench routing, depth, and slope verification
Underground and overhead conduit pathways
Openings, racks, hangers, and other structural elements requiring layout precision
Field verification of correct installation prior to backfill

Collect and record as-built data for installed components.
Verify layout accuracy through field checks, checklist, and coordination with BIM/CAD models and the project VDC team.
Support the project team in transferring layout data between Trimble equipment and design models.
Assist in organizing survey data files, control points, and field documentation.
Report discrepancies or field challenges to the Survey Superintendent or project management for resolution.
Maintain cleanliness, calibration, and functionality of all Trimble RTS and GPS equipment and accessories.
Follow company and project safety procedures for survey and layout activities within active construction zones.
Participate in daily and weekly project meetings as needed to understand upcoming layout needs.
Provide feedback to improve layout workflows, documentation, and field coordination processes.

Qualifications

3-5 years of experience in survey, layout, or related construction field work preferred.
Working knowledge of Trimble RTS and GPS systems, data collection, and layout procedures; training provided as needed.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, civil plans, and basic BIM/CAD layouts.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.
Ability to walk or stand on job sites for extended periods of time and lift up to 50 lbs.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites as required.

The inherent responsibilities of your role may include physical working conditions. In order to safely and successfully perform job duties you must be able to:
Potentially lift up to 50 pounds
Potentially need to do repeated pushing, pulling, carrying, reaching (or working above shoulder), walking, standing, sitting, stooping, kneeling, bending, and climbing
Potentially operate a motor vehicle, crane, tractor, etc.

We reserve the right to continually monitor your ability to safely and successfully complete these inherent physical responsibilities and take action as deemed appropriate in accordance with the Americans with Disability Act (ADA)

E&E promotes responsible management of resources, protects the environment, and implements effective and efficient policies for the benefit of Arkansas.

Job Summary

The Energy & Environment Program Coordinator oversees, develops, and implements environmental or energy-related programs for the State of Arkansas. This position is responsible for planning and directing resources to ensure the regulated community is in compliance with energy or environmental laws. This position is responsible for advancing programmatic goals that align with the department’s mission, coordinating regulatory or voluntary initiatives, supporting grant administration, and collaborating with stakeholders to ensure effective delivery of programs.

Primary Responsibilities

Manage statewide energy or environment programs. Serve as liaison between the state agency and stakeholders, including governmental bodies, the regulated community, and the public. Monitor and evaluate program performance, ensuring compliance with state rules and federal regulations and reporting requirements. Coordinate and manage grant applications, distribution of funds, and compliance tracking. Research, analyze, and interpret environmental data or energy trends to inform policy recommendations. Prepare technical reports, guidance documents, presentations, and educational materials for diverse audiences. Facilitate public meetings, stakeholder forums, and educational workshops. Promote equitable access to state energy or environmental regulatory resources through outreach and community engagement. Support the development of strategies to mitigate energy or environmental impacts. Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to support cross-agency initiatives. Provide general supervision of professional and administrative support staff by interviewing and recommending for hire, assigning and reviewing work, training new employees, and evaluating employee performance. Performance of other duties as assigned.

Knowledge And Skills

Ability to work independently, set programmatic goals, and manage multiple priorities. Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to convey complex information clearly to non-technical audiences.

Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with stakeholders across sectors.

Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and environmental data tools.

Adaptability: Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and adapting to shifting priorities or regulatory landscapes.

Commitment to transparency, public service, and environmentally responsible practices.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, conservation biology, natural resources management, or a related field. At least 2 years of experience in environmental or energy program coordination, with a focus on managing or supporting government projects.

Licensure/Certifications

N/A OTHER JOB RELATED EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE MAY BE SUBSTITUTED FOR ALL OR PART OF THESE BASIC REQUIREMENTS, EXCEPT FOR CERTIFICATION OR LICENSURE REQUIREMENTS, UPON APPROVAL OF THE QUALIFICATIONS REVIEW COMMITTEE.

Anticipated Job Duties

This position manages the Arkansas Energy Performance Contracting (AEPC) Program and Revolving Loan Lease Fund, serving as the main contact for public entities and ESCOs. Duties include RFP coordination, audit and contract reviews, project monitoring, loan coordination, among others. This role acts as a third-party owner's representative, ensuring proper communication throughout each project.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong communicator with experience distilling technical content and speaking to broad audiences
Solid understanding of ROI, amortization, contracts, and public financing tools like RLLFs or municipal bonds
Familiarity with construction, energy, or public sector projects with multiple stakeholders
Understanding of building energy-saving projects, including how they are planned, reviewed, and carried out in coordination with building owners and contractors

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator - Experiential Center
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Program Coordinator for the Experiential Center provides essential operational and logistical support to the Whitman Experiential Center, helping to implement student-centered, high-impact learning experiences at the Whitman School of Management. This role supports the execution of experiential initiatives by coordinating event logistics, managing communications, processing administrative tasks, and ensuring a high level of service to students and partners.

The coordinator works both collaboratively and independently, using sound judgment, attention to detail, and initiative to carry out responsibilities effectively. Success in this role requires a strong commitment to student engagement, the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, and the follow-through to ensure that programs are delivered smoothly and professionally.

This position is part of a bargaining unit and is represented by the union SEIU, Local 200United.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, education, or a related field and 2+ years of experience in program coordination, event planning, student services, or administrative support.
Or at least 5 years of experience in program management / coordination required.

Skills and Knowledge

Key Skills And Knowledge

Proven experience coordinating events or programs from planning through execution, with minimal oversight, demonstrating accuracy and attention to detail.
Experience managing budgets and financial processes, including expense tracking, budget reconciliation, and compliance with institutional policies.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build collaborative relationships with students, faculty, alumni, and external partners.
Ability to use sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and solve problems independently.
Self-starter with a proactive mindset and commitment to continuous improvement.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (especially Outlook, Excel, and Word); comfortable learning new systems.
Experience managing websites, databases, or online communication platforms.
Preferred Experience:
Experience working in a university setting, especially in roles related to event management, student engagement, or program management.
Comfort with basic data collection, assessment tools, or storytelling to support program evaluation and improvement.

Responsibilities

Program Coordination

Coordinate logistics for events, trips, competitions, and workshops, including space reservations, materials, catering, and AV needs.
Manage timelines and program calendars to ensure smooth execution and clear timely communication with stakeholders.
Support program planning by preparing agendas, managing checklists, and tracking action items.
Coordinate involvement of students, faculty, alumni, and industry partners to ensure meaningful engagement in programs.
Work with the Associate Director to assess and refine program models, contributing feedback based on execution.
Assist with data collection, reporting, and storytelling efforts to showcase program impact.

Operations And Administrative

Submit disbursement requests, travel authorizations, purchasing card transactions, and expense reports.
Coordinate travel logistics for programs, including group bookings, itineraries, and reimbursement.
Maintain and regularly update the Experiential Programs website with current opportunities and resources.
Organize files, documents, and records related to program operations.
Support budget tracking and reporting in collaboration with the associate director.

Student Communication And Engagement

Communicate with students to promote programs, answer questions, track participation, assess their experience, and distribute monetary awards as necessary.
Promote programs through multiple communication channels to drive student engagement.
Facilitate student participation in programs, ensuring equitable access and promoting hands-on involvement.
Assist in creating processes for student reflection, self-evaluation, peer evaluation, and/or supervisor evaluation.
Oversee student employees, including approving timecards and providing guidance as needed.

Other Duties

Participate in school events to represent experiential programs and student opportunities.
Support school-wide experiential learning events or cross-unit collaborations as needed.

Physical Requirements

NA

Tools/Equipment

NA

Application Instructions

In addition to completing an online application, please attach a resume and cover letter.

About Syracuse University

Syracuse University is a private, international research university with distinctive academics, diversely unique offerings, and an undeniable spirit. Located in the geographic heart of New York State, with a global footprint, and over 150 years of history, Syracuse University offers a quintessential college experience.

The scope of Syracuse University is a testament to its strengths: a pioneering history dating back to 1870; a choice of more than 200 majors, 100 minors, and 200 advanced degree programs offered across the University’s 13 schools and colleges; over 15,000 undergraduates and over 6,000 graduate students; more than a quarter of a million alumni in 160 countries; and a student population from all 50 U.S. states and 123 countries. For more information, please visit http://www.syracuse.edu.

About The Syracuse Area

Syracuse is a medium-sized city situated in the geographic center of New York State approximately 250 miles northwest of New York City. The metro-area population totals approximately 500,000. The area offers a low cost of living and provides many social, cultural, and recreational options, including parks, museums, festivals, professional regional theater, and premier shopping venues. Syracuse and Central New York present a wide range of seasonal recreation and attractions ranging from water skiing and snow skiing, hiking in the Adirondacks, touring the historic sites, visiting wineries along the Finger Lakes, and biking on trails along the Erie Canal.

EEO Statement

Syracuse University is an equal-opportunity institution. The University prohibits discrimination and harassment based on race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, ethnicity, marital status, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law to the extent prohibited by law. This nondiscrimination policy covers admissions, employment, and access to and treatment in University programs, services, and activities.

Commitment to Supporting and Hiring Veterans

Syracuse University has a long history of engaging veterans and the military-connected community through its educational programs, community outreach, and employment programs. After World War II, Syracuse University welcomed more than 10,000 returning veterans to our campus, and those veterans literally transformed Syracuse University into the national research institution it is today. The University’s contemporary commitment to veterans builds on this historical legacy, and extends to both class-leading initiatives focused on making an SU degree accessible and affordable to the post-9/11 generation of veterans, and also programs designed to position Syracuse University as the employer of choice for military veterans, members of the Guard and Reserve, and military family members.

Commitment to a Respectful and Welcoming Community

Syracuse University fosters a welcoming learning environment where students, faculty, administrators, staff, curriculum, social activities, governance, and all aspects of campus life reflect a broad range of perspectives and experiences. The University community values the many similarities and differences among individuals and groups. At Syracuse, we are committed to preparing students to engage with and appreciate the richness of backgrounds, beliefs, and experiences that shape our society. To achieve this, we strive to cultivate a community that respects and encourages open dialogue, understanding, and mutual respect.
